units.text: EXT. SALT FLAT - AFTERNOON
The ground is a white plate to every horizon, cracked into hexagons, and the sun sits on it like a coin on a table.
A sedan lies tipped in a drainage cut a quarter mile back, one wheel still turning in the heat.
IMOGEN REYES-HALL, fifties, sunburnt, a silk scarf knotted over her hair, drags a plastic jug by its handle across the crust.
Behind her, ABEL NKEMELU, twenty-six, limps with one shoe on and one shoe in his hand, his lips split and pale.
She stops.
He stops.
They look at the jug between them, the water in it barely above the lowest mark, and then at the horizon, which has not moved.
How far d'you think?
units.name: ABEL

units.text: To the highway? Eleven miles. Maybe nine.
units.name: IMOGEN

units.text: You said six this morning.
units.name: ABEL

units.text: This morning I was optimistic.
units.name: IMOGEN

units.text: And now?
units.name: ABEL

units.text: Now I can count. We have a pint each. We can walk at night, when it's cold, and sleep through the worst of the day under the car. That's what the book says. That's what I'd tell my students to do.
units.name: IMOGEN

units.text: You teach survival?
units.name: ABEL

units.text: I teach art history. I read a book once.
units.name: IMOGEN

units.text: God. Okay. Okay. Then why are we walking now?
units.name: ABEL

units.text: Because the car is a mile behind us and I could not make myself sit in it another hour. Because every minute I sat there I was listening for an engine.
units.name: IMOGEN

units.text: And?
units.name: ABEL

units.text: And there wasn't one. There was your breathing, and mine, and the metal ticking as it cooled. And I thought, if I stop moving I'll start counting, and if I start counting I'll know exactly how this ends.
units.name: IMOGEN

units.text: How does it end?
units.name: ABEL

units.text: You tell me. You're the one who wanted a shortcut.
units.name: IMOGEN

units.text: That's not fair.
units.name: ABEL

units.text: No. It isn't. I'm sorry.
units.name: IMOGEN

units.text: I saw the sign. I thought it said a gas station. It said a salt works. Closed. Since 1974.
units.name: ABEL

units.text: Abel. Stop.
units.name: IMOGEN

units.text: I'm just saying I read it wrong. Out loud. For the record. In case.
units.name: ABEL

units.text: In case what?
units.name: IMOGEN

units.text: In case one of us doesn't make it to the road, and the other one has to tell somebody.
units.name: ABEL

units.text: She lifts the jug and shoves it into his hands.
He holds it like something alive.
Drink. Two mouthfuls. Then I drink two. Then we walk until the sun touches the ground, and then we walk some more, and when we reach the road you can tell them any story you like.
units.name: IMOGEN

units.text: Two mouthfuls.
units.name: ABEL

units.text: He drinks.
Passes it.
She drinks.
Wipes her mouth with the back of her wrist and takes the jug, and they turn together toward the line where the white meets the sky.
